audit.cfg_summary: Straight-line target with three unconditional far calls, then one far return. No conditional, loop, switch or indirect branch occurs in this function.

call_map.effect: callee loads the 16-bit port and low value byte, then performs one OUT DX,AL

call_map.arguments: port 0x0205; value low byte of arithmetic f >> 4
port 0x0205; value low byte of (0x0f - arithmetic(vol >> 3)) + (channel_base + 0x80) + 0x10

reads: BP+0x08 signed word note; BP+0x0a signed word vol; BP+0x0c signed word chan. The first argument BP+0x06 (a) is never read.
Near word table g_75E8[note % 12], one 2-byte entry at base + 2*(note%12).
Port argument 0x0205 and byte value passed to f_29F0_002A; the helper reads its stack arguments and performs the port write.
writes: BP+0x0c argument cell is shifted left 5 in place; BP+0x0a is arithmetic-shifted right 3 and then overwritten by 0x0f minus that result. These are transient far-call argument-area words, matching the source parameter assignments; the behavioral harness intentionally excludes private call-stack bytes.
BP-0x02 stores f and BP-0x04 stores the channel-derived byte/word temporary. Frame and call-stack writes are restored/unwound.
No global data/table write. Exactly three ordered byte OUT effects to port 0x0205 through f_29F0_002A.
memory_state.state: No return value; no global state update; unused a has no load or side effect.

constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.widths_signedness: MSC int/parameters/table elements are signed 16-bit. note uses signed IDIV by 12 for quotient and remainder. Caller note 0..127 makes both nonnegative: remainder 0..11, quotient 0..10. Every g_75E8 entry is a positive word, so target SAR and source signed >> yield the same value. Caller byte velocity is passed as nonnegative int 0..255; arithmetic SAR 3 equals floor(vol/8). chan is 0..2, so chan<<5 is 0/32/64 and conversion to char remains nonnegative. Helper value is char/byte; only the low 8 bits are observable at OUT.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.pointer_math: No far/near pointer expression. Table addressing is 16-bit near base plus 2-byte signed-int element stride indexed by remainder 0..11.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.constants: channel scale 5 bits (<<5); note divisor/table length 12; frequency mask 0x0f; channel register base 0x80; volume register offset 0x10; volume inversion 0x0f; port 0x0205; helper value writes are 8-bit.

static_axes.algorithm: The source and original derive the semitone frequency from the same table and signed quotient shift; write its low nibble with channel base, write remaining frequency bits shifted by four, then invert the 3-bit volume level and write the channel volume register.
static_axes.control_flow: All instructions are accounted for in a straight-line CFG. Three unconditional calls remain in source order; no branch or alternate return exists.
static_axes.calls: Each call is f_29F0_002A(port=0x0205,value=low byte). Its pinned disassembly at root:29F0:002A is exactly one OUT DX,AL between argument loads and far return; thus three one-byte writes occur in the same order.
static_axes.memory: Table word read, parameter argument-area stores, two local stack temporaries and call frames are accounted for. No global data writes.
static_axes.return_abi: void far; frame and far return restored; a unused.
static_axes.completeness_basis: Static reconstruction uses complete 120-byte original context and full registered module source/types/table values; the caller-domain bounds establish safe table and shift ranges. Differential output is only corroborating evidence.

review_notes: The accepted caller domain is channel 0..2, MIDI note 0..127 and byte velocity 0..255. The 60 wider/out-of-domain robustness probes are diagnostic only; invalid negative/out-of-table notes and host acoustic/timing equivalence are excluded.

Original code stores chan and vol back into their transient argument stack slots. The static inventory records both writes; the harness contract excludes private call-stack bytes, so its pass is not evidence for those bytes. Under the C ABI they are parameter working storage, not a caller-owned persistent object.

Run provenance check: source_sha256 pins the 43b2... module bytes; compiled_source_sha256 is cd00..., exactly SHA-256 of the same file after Python universal-newline normalization (111 CRLF sequences -> LF). The reviewed harness hashes read_bytes for source_sha256 but read_text/normalized text after unscaffold for compiled_source_sha256; this source contains no SCAFFOLD block. Thus the two digests identify the same body, not a different candidate.
